CHAPTER V
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Article 12
Obligations and responsibilities in the implementation of protection for children and women victims of violence are the shared responsibility of:
a. regional government;
b. community;
c. family and parents.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Konawe Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Konawe Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Konawe.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Konawe Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb.
7. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes a person who is legally recognized as a Woman.
8. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, sexual abuse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
15. Victim is a child and woman who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-strengthening of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced.
21. Repatriation is an effort to return child and woman victims of violence to family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, or substitute family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
24. Institution is an agency/office/body/bureau within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance.
25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Center Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter, etc.
26. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in the context of implementing prevention and protection activities for women and children victims of violence.
27. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

CHAPTER VI I
REPORTING
Article 26
(1) PPT reports the implementation of the provision of protection for children and women victims of violence to the Regent.
(2) Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted in writing, covering:
a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
(3) Submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

Article 18
(1) In carrying out its duties and functions, the PPT may coordinate with the Sub-district PPT and competent parties in conducting efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence against children and women.
(2) Further provisions regarding the mechanism for implementing the prevention duties as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 25
The guidance and supervision as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (2) and paragraph (3), shall be carried out in order to realize the objectives of providing protection for children and women victims of violence in accordance with the minimum service standards established by laws and regulations.

Article 16
(1) In order to provide services and protection to children and women from violence, the Regional Government establishes PPT as an integrated service center for children and women victims of violence.
(2) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of elements from the Health Office, Youth Education and Sports Office, Social Office, Cooperatives Industry and Trade Office, Population and Civil Registration Office, Women's Empowerment and Family Planning Agency, Community Empowerment Agency, Civil Service Police Unit, Regional General Hospital, Resort Police, Non-Governmental Organizations, and Universities.
(3) PPT as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be established by Regent's decree.
(4) The provision of services to victims shall be carried out in an integrated manner by PPT.
(5) PPT as referred to in paragraph (4) may receive and send case referrals from or to other service units in a networked manner.
(6) PPT provides services and temporary protection in the form of safe houses.
(7) In the event that PPT does not yet have a safe house, then victims of violence shall be referred to PPT that has a safe house.
(8) PPT consists of several counseling fields.
(9) The counseling fields as referred to in paragraph (8) shall at minimum consist of:
a. legal field;
b. health field;
c. spiritual field; and
d. psychology field.
(10) Further provisions regarding the organizational structure of PPT shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

CHAPTER VI
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 24
(1) Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for children and women victims of violence.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
(3) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), is conducted with the principles of:
a. professional;
b. transparent; and
c. accountable.

REGENT OF KONAWE
DECIDES:
To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION OF KONAWE REGENCY ON THE PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE IN KONAWE REGENCY

Article 20
(1) In carrying out service duties for children and women victims of violence, PPT coordinates with the Sub-district PPT.
(2) The mechanism for implementing the duties as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in accordance with Standard Operating Procedures, which are further regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 15
The obligations of the family and parents as referred to in Article 11 letter c, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and to protect children and women as members of the family.

Article 28
(1) Regional Governments may provide financing assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or non-governmental organizations and universities that carry out protection for children and women victims of violence.
(2) Financing assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

Article 17
Forms of prevention of violence against children and women carried out by PPT, can be implemented through:
a. Socialization activities of laws and regulations to the community related to the protection of the rights of children and women; and
b. Training of PPT members related to the implementation of their duties in preventing violence against children and women.

CHAPTER VII
FUNDING
Article 27
Funds for the implementation of protection of children and women victims of violence, are sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

4.2.rationale: While the Indonesian text mentions socialization of women’s rights (Pasal 17 huruf a; Pasal 14 ayat (2) huruf c), it does not specifically require 'gender equality education' (pendidikan kesetaraan gender) or education aimed at transforming gender norms/roles; it is framed as socialization of laws/rights and general prevention. The judge treated women’s-rights socialization as equivalent to gender-equality education ('though not explicitly framed as gender equality') and still answered Yes. Given the indicator is specifically about gender equality education, the more accurate label based on the Indonesian text is No, so the judge overgeneralized from available passages.

Article 18
(1) In carrying out its duties and functions, the PPT may coordinate with the Sub-district PPT and competent parties in conducting efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence against children and women.
(2) Further provisions regarding the mechanism for implementing the prevention duties as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 15
The obligations of the family and parents as referred to in Article 11 letter c, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and to protect children and women as members of the family.

Article 17
Forms of prevention of violence against children and women carried out by PPT, can be implemented through:
a. Socialization activities of laws and regulations to the community related to the protection of the rights of children and women; and
b. Training of PPT members related to the implementation of their duties in preventing violence against children and women.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Konawe Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Konawe Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Konawe.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Konawe Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb.
7. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes a person who is legally recognized as a Woman.
8. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, sexual abuse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
15. Victim is a child and woman who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-strengthening of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced.
21. Repatriation is an effort to return child and woman victims of violence to family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, or substitute family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
24. Institution is an agency/office/body/bureau within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance.
25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Center Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter, etc.
26. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in the context of implementing prevention and protection activities for women and children victims of violence.
27. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

Article 25
The guidance and supervision as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (2) and paragraph (3), shall be carried out in order to realize the objectives of providing protection for children and women victims of violence in accordance with the minimum service standards established by laws and regulations.

Article 16
(1) In order to provide services and protection to children and women from violence, the Regional Government establishes PPT as an integrated service center for children and women victims of violence.
(2) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of elements from the Health Office, Youth Education and Sports Office, Social Office, Cooperatives Industry and Trade Office, Population and Civil Registration Office, Women's Empowerment and Family Planning Agency, Community Empowerment Agency, Civil Service Police Unit, Regional General Hospital, Resort Police, Non-Governmental Organizations, and Universities.
(3) PPT as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be established by Regent's decree.
(4) The provision of services to victims shall be carried out in an integrated manner by PPT.
(5) PPT as referred to in paragraph (4) may receive and send case referrals from or to other service units in a networked manner.
(6) PPT provides services and temporary protection in the form of safe houses.
(7) In the event that PPT does not yet have a safe house, then victims of violence shall be referred to PPT that has a safe house.
(8) PPT consists of several counseling fields.
(9) The counseling fields as referred to in paragraph (8) shall at minimum consist of:
a. legal field;
b. health field;
c. spiritual field; and
d. psychology field.
(10) Further provisions regarding the organizational structure of PPT shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Article 28
(1) Regional Governments may provide financing assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or non-governmental organizations and universities that carry out protection for children and women victims of violence.
(2) Financing assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

CHAPTER VI
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 24
(1) Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for children and women victims of violence.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
(3) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), is conducted with the principles of:
a. professional;
b. transparent; and
c. accountable.

Article 20
(1) In carrying out service duties for children and women victims of violence, PPT coordinates with the Sub-district PPT.
(2) The mechanism for implementing the duties as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in accordance with Standard Operating Procedures, which are further regulated by a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER V
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Article 12
Obligations and responsibilities in the implementation of protection for children and women victims of violence are the shared responsibility of:
a. regional government;
b. community;
c. family and parents.

CHAPTER VII
FUNDING
Article 27
Funds for the implementation of protection of children and women victims of violence, are sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VI I
REPORTING
Article 26
(1) PPT reports the implementation of the provision of protection for children and women victims of violence to the Regent.
(2) Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted in writing, covering:
a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
(3) Submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

CHAPTER VI
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION
Part One
Institutional

Article 5
Physical violence as referred to in Article 4 letter a is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, serious injury or disability to a person's body, miscarriage (loss of pregnancy), fainting and/or cause death.

4.4.rationale: The Indonesian regulation explicitly uses education/training as prevention: Pasal 17 states forms of prevention by PPT include (a) community 'sosialisasi' of relevant laws/regulations and (b) 'pelatihan anggota PPT' regarding their duties in preventing violence against children and women. These are prevention-through-education/training measures. The retrieved English passage [4.4-21] reflects Pasal 17, and the judge’s reasoning aligns with the Indonesian text. Therefore the golden label 'No' appears incorrect.
